summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a tibetologist who completed her PhD at SOAS University of London between circa 2000 and 2004 under doctoral supervisor Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Yannick Laurent specializes in tibetology and history/archaeology. In 2026, he is attested holding posts at the University of Munich and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taixu from circa 1934 to 1939 and under Yinshun from circa 1941 to 1945.
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of tibetology and sinology. He studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010) under the supervision of Xue Yu.

Yaroslav Komarovski is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at various Tibetan monastic institutes, the University of Virginia, and Washington University in St. Louis, he became Professor at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln in 2009.

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University (1961–1967), he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography, and became Chief Researcher at Kunstkamera in 2005.

Yashaswini Chandra is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She held positions at SOAS, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Sahapedia (2011–2018), Ashoka University (2019), and the University of Edinburgh (2023).

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta, later serving as professor at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a linguist and tibetologist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD circa 1977–1983). He held professorships at the National Museum of Ethnology and executive roles at NIHU and SOKENDAI.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar in philosophy and sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and has served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and held teaching posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed short-term study at Tübingen University Library and worked at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1983–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2022).

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who is attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Ueno works in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004), holding a post there as well as a research fellow position at Koyasan University in 2004.

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1978–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen (PhD ~1973). He held faculty posts at Kindai University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Kyoto University.

Yasuko Kojima is a scholar in tibetology and linguistics attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
